dedupe_keys.name: pssim matlab power system dynamic simulator

description: PSSim is a MATLAB-based power system dynamic simulator for research and teaching on power system dynamics and control. It was created by the SPEED lab at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, directed by Hector Pulgar, with contributors Sebastian Martinez-Lizana and Francisco Zelaya-Arrazabal, and version 1.0 was released in March 2025 and archived on Zenodo in April 2025. It performs power flow analysis, time-domain RMS simulation and small-signal stability analysis, and shows basic simulator structures, models and practices drawn from open-source and commercial software, so that users can develop and test new control and analysis methods. The authors state it is not meant to replace other simulators. Coverage is not tied to a place. The code is accessible on GitHub and Zenodo at no cost, under CC BY 4.0 as stated on Zenodo. Caveats: MATLAB is needed, no licence file is in the repository, and there is only one release. Simulation uses are dynamic stability studies after faults and disturbances and controller testing. Related records: model-power-system-small-signal-tool-manchester and model-frecol-frequency-control-toolbox are other MATLAB dynamics tools.
